chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani, who said:

I wrote to him while I was in al-Madinah, asking him about the day concerning which there is doubt as to whether it is from the month of Ramadan: should it be fasted or not? So he wrote: Certainty is not entered by doubt. Fast upon sighting, and break the fast upon sighting.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Tusi said: The reports in this chapter are too many to be counted. We have cited a large portion of them in our major book, and have limited ourselves here to the amount that we have mentioned so that the book may not become too lengthy.

key_terms.أَفْطِرْ: break the fast; end fasting based on sighting
key_terms.الشَّكُّ: doubt regarding whether the day belongs to Ramadan
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارُ: narrations or reports on the subject
key_terms.الْيَقِينُ: certainty that is not displaced by mere doubt
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose beginning is under discussion
key_terms.صُمْ: fast; the command to begin fasting based on sighting
key_terms.لِلرُّؤْيَةِ: upon sighting; meaning the sighting of the new moon

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the doubtful day before Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report states the ruling regarding the doubtful day at the beginning of Ramadan: certainty is not overturned by doubt, so fasting and ending the fast are tied to moon-sighting. The closing note from al-Tusi indicates that many narrations exist on this legal issue and that only a selection is cited here.
